sn54.16:3.3: Just mindful, they breathe in. Mindful, they breathe out. …
sn54.16:3.4: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing letting go.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing letting go.’
sn54.16:4.1: There’s a time when a mendicant is breathing in heavily, and they know: ‘I’m breathing in heavily.’ Breathing out heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing out heavily.’ Breathing in lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing in lightly.’ …
sn54.16:4.3: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the physical process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the physical process.’
sn54.16:4.4: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:4.6: Because the breath is a certain aspect of the body, I say.
sn54.16:4.7: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:5.1: There’s a time when a mendicant is experiencing rapture …
sn54.16:5.4: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in stilling the mental process.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out stilling the mental process.’
sn54.16:5.5: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:5.7: Because careful application of mind to the in-breaths and out-breaths is a certain aspect of feelings, I say.
sn54.16:5.8: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:6.1: There’s a time when a mendicant is experiencing the mind …
sn54.16:6.3: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in immersing the mind in samādhi.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out immersing the mind in samādhi.’
sn54.16:6.4: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in freeing the mind.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out freeing the mind.’
sn54.16:6.5: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:6.7: Because there is no development of immersion due to mindfulness of breathing for someone who is unmindful and lacks awareness, I say.
sn54.16:6.8: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of the mind—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:7.1: There’s a time when a mendicant is observing impermanence …
sn54.16:7.4: They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe in observing letting go.’ They practice like this: ‘I’ll breathe out observing letting go.’
sn54.16:7.5: At such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:7.6: Having seen with wisdom the giving up of covetousness and displeasure, they closely watch over it with equanimity.
sn54.16:7.7: Therefore, at such a time a mendicant is meditating by observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
sn54.16:8.1: That’s how immersion due to mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
sn54.16:9.1: And how are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors?
sn54.16:9.2: Whenever a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body, their mindfulness is established and lucid.
sn54.16:9.3: At such a time a mendicant’s mindfulness is established and lucid.
sn54.16:9.4: At that time the awakening factor of mindfulness has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness; and at that time the awakening factor of mindfulness comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:10.1: As they live mindfully in this way they investigate, explore, and inquire into that principle with wisdom.
sn54.16:10.2: At such a time a mendicant who lives mindfully in this way investigates, explores, and inquires into that principle with wisdom.
sn54.16:10.3: At that time the awakening factor of investigation of principles has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of investigation of principles; and at that time the awakening factor of investigation of principles comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:11.1: As they investigate, explore, and inquire into that principle with wisdom, their energy is roused up and unflagging.
sn54.16:11.2: At such a time, as a mendicant investigates, explores, and inquires into that principle with wisdom, their energy is roused up and unflagging.
sn54.16:11.3: At that time the awakening factor of energy has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of energy; and at that time the awakening factor of energy comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:12.1: Rapture not of the flesh arises in someone whose energy is roused up.
sn54.16:12.2: At such a time rapture not of the flesh arises in a mendicant whose energy is roused up.
sn54.16:12.3: At that time the awakening factor of rapture has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of rapture; and at that time the awakening factor of rapture comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:13.1: When the mind is full of rapture, both body and mind become tranquil.
sn54.16:13.2: At such a time, when a mendicant’s mind is full of rapture, both body and mind become tranquil.
sn54.16:13.3: At that time the awakening factor of tranquility has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of tranquility; and at that time the awakening factor of tranquility comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:14.1: When the body is tranquil and one feels bliss, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.
sn54.16:14.2: At such a time, when a mendicant’s body is tranquil and they feel bliss, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.
sn54.16:14.3: At that time the awakening factor of immersion has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of immersion; and at that time the awakening factor of immersion comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:15.1: They closely watch over that mind immersed in samādhi.
sn54.16:15.2: At such a time a mendicant closely watches over the mind so immersed in samādhi.
sn54.16:15.3: At that time the awakening factor of equanimity has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of equanimity; and at that time the awakening factor of equanimity comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:16.1: Whenever a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of feelings …
sn54.16:16.3: Whenever a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of principles, their mindfulness is established and lucid.
sn54.16:16.4: At such a time a mendicant’s mindfulness is established and lucid.
sn54.16:16.5: At that time the awakening factor of mindfulness has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness; and at that time the awakening factor of mindfulness comes to perfection through development …
sn54.16:17.1: They closely watch over that mind immersed in samādhi.
sn54.16:17.2: At such a time a mendicant closely watches over the mind so immersed in samādhi.
sn54.16:17.3: At that time the awakening factor of equanimity has been activated by the mendicant; at that time the mendicant develops the awakening factor of equanimity; and at that time the awakening factor of equanimity comes to perfection through development.
sn54.16:17.4: That’s how the four kinds of mindfulness meditation are developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors.
sn54.16:18.1: And how are the seven awakening factors developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and freedom?
sn54.16:18.2: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.
sn54.16:18.3: They develop the awakening factor of investigation of principles, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go …
sn54.16:18.4: They develop the awakening factor of equanimity, which relies on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripens as letting go.
